desk_read: Yesterday saw heavy selling across equities and industrial metals, led by a 3.29% drop in Natural Gas alongside 1.3x its 20-day average volume in a contango curve. Copper and Silver also faced steep price declines of 1.70% and 1.89% respectively, supported by elevated volume at 1.5x and 1.3x the 20-day average in contango structures. Meanwhile, Gold ticked up 0.03% on heavy volume at 1.4x its 20-day average with a contango curve, while Brent managed a fractional 0.02% gain at 0.9x average volume in backwardation. Total net flows across these sessions remain undefined by single-contract changes as open-interest shifts show zero net movement on individual leads, leaving the broader complex to digest these volume surges without clear directional build.
oil_read: WTI edged down -0.20% with volume at 0.9x its 20-day average, while Brent (NYMEX) gained +0.02% on volume also at 0.9x its 20-day average. Both markets maintained backwardation, highlighted by the CLZ26-CLK27 spread at +7.03 $/bbl and the BZF27-BZM27 spread at +9.69 $/bbl. Furthermore, the Brent (NYMEX) minus WTI delivery month F27 spread stood at +8.55 $/bbl.
bias_read: WTI Crude Oil shows a neutral bias with the curve in backwardation, while Brent sits at mildly bullish with backwardation steepening, suggesting positioning supports the move without signaling overextension. Natural Gas registers a mildly bearish bias where price fell without an open-interest reading on volume at 1.3x the 20-day average, showing conviction that warns of a deeper downward trend. Silver and Copper also display mildly bearish biases with prices down without open-interest readings on volume at 1.3x and 1.5x the 20-day average respectively, meaning strong volume backs the weakness. Overall, the mixed neutral and directional flows point to selective conviction in commodities while equities remain sidelined.
